The **AvtoVAZ Technical Museum** (Russian: *Технический музей ОАО «АВТОВАЗ»*) is a unique automotive and industrial museum located in **Tolyatti, Russia**, dedicated to the history of **AvtoVAZ** (the manufacturer of **Lada** cars) and Soviet/Russian automotive and industrial technology. Here’s everything I know about it:

---

### **1. Overview & Location**
- **Full Name:** AvtoVAZ Technical Museum (Технический музей ОАО «АВТОВАЗ»)
- **Location:** Tolyatti, Samara Oblast, Russia (within the AvtoVAZ industrial complex)
- **Founded:** 1998 (officially opened to the public in 2001)
- **Founder:** AvtoVAZ (the company behind Lada cars)
- **Purpose:** To preserve and showcase the history of AvtoVAZ, Soviet/Russian automotive engineering, and industrial achievements.

---

### **2. History & Background**
- AvtoVAZ was established in **1966** as a joint venture between the Soviet government and **Fiat** (Italy) to produce affordable cars for the Soviet masses.
- The museum was created to document the **evolution of Lada (VAZ) cars**, as well as other Soviet-era vehicles and industrial equipment.
- It serves as both a **corporate museum** and a **public exhibition space**, attracting car enthusiasts, historians, and tourists.

---

### **3. Exhibits & Collections**
The museum houses a vast collection of **vehicles, engines, prototypes, and industrial machinery**, including:

#### **A. Lada (VAZ) Cars & Prototypes**
- **Early Models:**
  - **VAZ-2101 (Zhiguli / Lada 1200)** – The first Lada, based on the Fiat 124 (1970).
  - **VAZ-2103, VAZ-2106** – Luxury versions of the original Lada.
  - **VAZ-2105/2107 (Lada Riva)** – Classic Soviet sedans.
- **Experimental & Concept Cars:**
  - **VAZ-1111 Oka** – A microcar (1988).
  - **VAZ-2120 Nadezhda** – A rare minivan (1998).
  - **VAZ-2110 (Lada 110)** – Early prototypes and pre-production models.
  - **VAZ-2123 (Chevrolet Niva prototype)** – The precursor to the modern Niva.
  - **Lada Revolution** – A sports car concept (2003).
  - **Lada Vesta & XRAY prototypes** – Modern Lada models.
- **Racing & Special Editions:**
  - **Lada VFTS** – A rally version of the VAZ-2105 (used in Soviet motorsports).
  - **Lada Samara T3** – A Dakar Rally prototype (1990s).
  - **Lada Granta & Vesta WTCC race cars** – Modern touring car versions.

#### **B. Soviet & Russian Military & Industrial Vehicles**
- **UAZ-469** – Iconic Soviet off-road military vehicle.
- **GAZ-69** – Another classic Soviet military jeep.
- **ZIL & GAZ trucks** – Heavy-duty Soviet-era trucks.
- **KAMAZ & Ural trucks** – Modern Russian military and civilian trucks.
- **Armored vehicles & tanks** – Some military prototypes and models.

#### **C. Aircraft & Aviation**
- **MiG-21** – Soviet fighter jet (full-scale model).
- **Yak-40** – Soviet passenger jet (cockpit section).
- **Helicopters (Mi-2, Mi-8)** – Soviet-era rotorcraft.

#### **D. Space & Rocket Technology**
- **Soyuz rocket engine** – A real RD-107 engine used in Soviet space missions.
- **Lunar rover models** – Soviet space exploration prototypes.
- **Satellite & spacecraft components** – Including parts from the **Buran space shuttle program**.

#### **E. Industrial & Engineering Exhibits**
- **AvtoVAZ production line models** – Miniature replicas of the Tolyatti factory.
- **Robotics & automation** – Early Soviet industrial robots.
- **Engines & transmissions** – From Lada cars to aircraft and rockets.
- **Welding & manufacturing tools** – Used in Soviet car production.

#### **F. Foreign Cars (Comparative Exhibits)**
- **Fiat 124** – The original car that inspired the VAZ-2101.
- **Renault & Nissan models** – Since Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi now owns a stake in AvtoVAZ.
- **Other Soviet-era cars (Moskvitch, ZAZ, GAZ)** – For historical context.

---

### **4. Unique & Rare Exhibits**
- **VAZ-2101 "Kopeyka" (1970)** – The very first Lada ever produced.
- **VAZ-2108 "Sputnik" (1984)** – The first front-wheel-drive Lada.
- **VAZ-2121 "Niva" (1977)** – The original off-road Lada, still in production today.
- **Lada 111 (1995)** – A rare station wagon prototype.
- **Lada Kalina & Priora prototypes** – Early development models.
- **Soviet-era microcars (ZAZ-965, SMZ S-3D)** – Tiny city cars from the USSR.

---

### **5. Museum Layout & Features**
- **Main Exhibition Hall** – Displays cars, trucks, and industrial equipment.
- **Outdoor Area** – Features larger vehicles (trucks, tanks, aircraft).
- **Interactive Displays** – Some exhibits allow visitors to sit in cars or operate controls.
- **Archive & Library** – Contains historical documents, blueprints, and photos.
- **Gift Shop** – Sells Lada memorabilia, books, and model cars.

---

### **6. Visitor Information**
- **Address:** Ulitsa Yuzhnoye Shosse, 36, Tolyatti, Samara Oblast, Russia (inside the AvtoVAZ factory complex).
- **Opening Hours:**
  - Typically **Tuesday–Sunday (10:00 AM – 6:00 PM)**.
  - Closed on **Mondays** and some holidays.
- **Admission Fees:**
  - Around **200–500 RUB** (varies for adults, students, and children).
  - Guided tours may cost extra.
- **How to Get There:**
  - **By Car:** Located near the AvtoVAZ factory (about 15 km from central Tolyatti).
  - **By Public Transport:** Buses and marshrutkas (shared taxis) run from Tolyatti’s city center.
- **Best Time to Visit:** Weekdays (fewer crowds) or during special automotive events.

---

### **7. Special Events & Activities**
- **Car Shows & Rallies** – The museum hosts classic car meets and Lada enthusiast gatherings.
- **Restoration Workshops** – Some exhibits are restored on-site.
- **Educational Programs** – For school groups and engineering students.
- **Temporary Exhibitions** – Featuring new Lada models or guest vehicles.

---

### **8. Why Visit?**
✅ **For Car Enthusiasts** – A must-see for fans of **Soviet/Russian automotive history**.
✅ **For History Buffs** – Learn about **Soviet industrialization and space race technology**.
✅ **For Families** – Interactive exhibits and outdoor displays make it fun for kids.
✅ **For Photographers** – Unique vintage cars, aircraft, and industrial machinery.
✅ **For Lada Owners** – A pilgrimage site for those who love classic Ladas.

---

### **9. Nearby Attractions**
- **AvtoVAZ Factory Tour** – Some tours include a visit to the **Lada production line**.
- **Tolyatti City Museum** – Local history and culture.
- **Volga River Embankment** – Scenic views and parks.
- **Stavropol-on-Volga** – A nearby historic town.

---

### **10. Interesting Facts**
- The museum is **one of the largest automotive museums in Russia**.
- Some exhibits are **one-of-a-kind prototypes** that never went into mass production.
- The **Soyuz rocket engine** on display is a **real flown artifact**.
- The **Lada Niva** is the **longest-running car model in continuous production** (since 1977).
- The museum has **collaborated with other automotive museums** in Russia and Europe.

---

### **11. Online Presence & Contact**
- **Official Website:** [AvtoVAZ Technical Museum (in Russian)](http://www.tm-avtovaz.ru/)
- **Social Media:** Some updates are posted on **VK (VKontakte)** and **Instagram**.
- **Phone:** +7 (8482) 75-75-75 (AvtoVAZ general contact; ask for the museum).

---

### **12. Tips for Visitors**
✔ **Bring ID** – The museum is inside a factory complex, so security may check documents.
✔ **Book a Guided Tour** – Some exhibits are explained better with a guide.
✔ **Check for Events** – Some days have special exhibitions or car shows.
✔ **Combine with a Factory Tour** – If possible, visit the **Lada assembly line** nearby.
✔ **Photography Allowed** – But check for restrictions in certain areas.

---

### **Final Thoughts**
The **AvtoVAZ Technical Museum** is a **hidden gem** for anyone interested in **Soviet/Russian automotive history, industrial engineering, or space technology**. It’s not just about Ladas—it’s a **time capsule of Soviet innovation**, from cars to rockets. If you’re in **Tolyatti**, it’s a **must-visit**!
